sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. LAPL is a concentrated automotive motor/lighting supplier with real FY26 volume growth and strong accounting-based incremental returns, but persistent poor cash conversion and unresolved controls prevent a favorable investment conclusion. BQS 5.3 and capped GQS 5.0 are diagnostic only; IAS is NS. The ₹118.70 reference is secondary and non-executable; funding and tradability remain unverified. This is a small industrial growth/capacity-ramp thesis, not an established compounder. The strongest positive is motor/lighting volume growth with a stable organic capital bridge; the decisive risks are 77.18% single-customer dependence, earnings that do not turn into cash, and unsettled financial controls. A clean post-IPO liquidity and audit reconciliation could change the evidence state. A lower share price alone cannot resolve these gates. This is research, not a trade or a personalized allocation.

The research uses restated FY23–26 and separately labeled original FY21–22. Identity/share-count confidence high; reported/restated arithmetic high but reliability medium/low under G2; operating unit economics medium; present financing/tradability low. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold and G4 Hold have separate meanings and resolution conditions. The ₹5 lakh position is an illustration only, not suitable-allocation advice.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 factor scores are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP 7, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 7, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. BQS is exactly 5.26, displayed 5.3. GQS raw 6.40 is capped to 5.00 because CASH 3 reflects persistent poor cash realization, not a one-period investment build. IAS has 45% known weight: quality 1.315 plus downside 0.600=1.915; missing 55% produces arithmetic 1–10 factor bounds 2.465–7.415, not a score or confidence interval. No neutral imputation is used. All rankings are excluded under G2 pending resolution; computable historical factors are not discarded simply because live investment evidence is missing. GOV 4 does not trigger the≤3 governance cap; G3 is Hold rather than demonstrated funding failure, so no invented distressed cap. With REV 8 under the five-year alternative BQS would 5.38 and raw GQS 6.80, still capped 5.0; classification unchanged. One-point GOV/MOAT changes move BQS 0.20 each, CAP/REV 0.12, CASH/DUR 0.10, BAL/EXEC 0.08. No after-the-fact undocumented haircut is applied.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: LAPL makes automotive motors, lamps/lighting, mirrors, hoods and related components at its Aurangabad-area units. Manufacturing adds design/tooling, molding, assembly and qualification to purchased materials, then converts OEM call-offs to production and trade receivables. FY26 product sales were motor ₹55.1134 cr, lighting ₹31.7114 cr, mirrors ₹0.4633 cr, hoods ₹0.9922 cr and other ₹4.6351 cr. These total ₹92.9154 cr; the ₹0.3363 cr difference to revenue from operations is other operating revenue, not unallocated product orders. Motor/light shares are 59.32%/34.13% of product sales. Largest customer 77.18%, top 3 86.72% and top 10 95.49%; customer identity is not inferred from logos or industry familiarity. Company disclosures do not establish guaranteed long-term minimum purchases. Most sales are domestic; exact end-OEM/aftermarket export economics are not independently segmented. Material input ₹65.1754 cr and top 10 suppliers 59.66% create raw-material and procurement concentration. Revenue is therefore a function of customer platform production, LAPL content and share per platform, realization/mix, and collection terms, rather than an automatically recurring subscription.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: Process knowledge, OEM qualification, tooling and proximity can make replacement inconvenient, but the evidence supports a useful supplier relationship rather than a structural pricing moat. The largest buyer’s 77.18% share has barely changed from 76.90% in FY24; no customer-specific contract length, termination protection, tooling ownership or negotiated pass-through lag is disclosed sufficiently to quantify switching economics. Motor capacity 90.70% and lighting 91.25% utilization show demand but also little slack. Fiem, Minda Corporation and Lumax Industries are relevant, imperfect comparators: Fiem’s lighting focus is closest; Minda spans more electrical/component categories; Lumax has larger automotive-lighting engineering and partnership resources. S1 reports FY26 consolidated revenue ₹2815.6087 cr for Fiem and ₹6185.34 cr for Minda, versus LAPL ₹93.2517 cr; their prospectus EBITDA definitions include other income and are not silently equated with LAPL operating EBITDA. Lumax’s directly inspected FY26 standalone highlights report ₹4184 cr revenue, ₹412 cr EBITDA and ₹146 cr PAT,12 plants and a long Stanley technology relationship. Those scales are roughly 30×/66×/45× LAPL, so their historic valuation multiples cannot simply be assigned to it. ACMA’s January 2026 review reports 6.8% industry growth and 7.3% OEM-supply growth in H1 FY26. This supports a real market, not a claim that LAPL can access every rupee of sector TAM. Failure modes include platform loss, tooling obsolescence, annual buyer price reductions, material shortages and EV architecture change.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text: FY21–26 reported revenue is ₹33.0709/43.9117/60.0748/60.7348/65.9753/93.2517 cr. Absolute FY24/FY25/FY26 additions are ₹0.6600/5.2405/27.2764 cr, so the newest year, not a smooth historical compounding pattern, produces most acceleration. The five-year 23.04% CAGR is shown but not selected: FY21 is a pandemic-disrupted original-statements base, FY22 had a fire disruption, and older years are not supplied on the full IPO-restated basis. The selected FY23–26 restated/normalized-demand window gives 15.79%, mapping directly to REV 7 with no extra trajectory or small-base adjustment. This is a disclosed measurement choice; REV 8 is the five-year sensitivity, not suppressed evidence. No ten-year comparable series or four-quarter FY27 series is available. FY26 motor monthly production rose 80,899→136,058, about 68.18%, with sales+40.84%; lighting 143,744→205,322, 42.84%, with sales+35.01%. Production-normalized sales per unit consequently fell: motor about ₹403→₹338 and lighting ₹136→₹129. These are not invoiced ASPs because stock movements and product mix differ, but they contradict a claim that price increases alone drove revenue. No acquisition contribution is identified. FY26 growth is thus substantially volume-led, with unresolved mix/realization detail and extreme customer dependence.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The bottom-up path is debottlenecking motor/lighting output, adding Unit IV capacity and qualifying new products/customers. A mirror line at 61.78% utilization has spare capacity; a simple 81.24% average across three categories does not mean every line has 19% spare output. The remaining project estimate is ₹22.3549 cr, funded by ₹19.56 cr earmarked IPO money and ₹2.7949 cr internal accrual/debt; ₹3.5932 cr land is already paid and embedded in operating assets. The net-proceeds timetable allocates ₹9.78 cr in each of FY27/FY28. Quotes were not firm purchase orders, and taxes/extra costs are not covered by a fabricated fixed-price promise. Construction began 19 August; new vendor codes grant eligibility to bid, not contracted revenue. The model assumes gradual growth and FY29 contribution after spending, deliberately distinguishing deployment from qualification/ramp. Base FY27 growth 18% exceeds the roughly 9–10% physical headroom in the existing motor/lighting lines; it requires extra shifts, debottlenecking or higher-value mix before Unit IV. This is an execution-dependent assumption, not output assured by existing capacity; the bear case starts at zero growth. Core operating capital rose ₹33.063 cr over FY23–26 while normalized NOPAT rose ₹8.1142 cr, giving 24.54%; two-year 27.74% and alternative funded-capital 25.34%/26.49% support CAP 7 versus 14–18% capital costs. This valid aggregate substitute has a stable organic perimeter, includes work in progress and inventory/receivables, and is not a project IRR. The cash-investment-to-book-IC residual−₹0.1725 cr is retained rather than solved by assumption. New plant returns may differ, and persistent cash conversion caps GQS at 5 despite raw 6.4. A broad EV opportunity cannot erase these financing and realization constraints.

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text: Promoters are Neeraj Satyaprakash Goyal, Shubham Neeraj Goyal and Anita Neeraj Goyal. The analysis evaluates documented conduct rather than surname or family ownership. Historic conversion/allotment, rights-timing and related statutory documentation lapses led to a compounding application dated 16 May 2026, still pending in the 11 August prospectus. Management calls the lapses inadvertent and describes corrective filings; no completed adjudication is assumed. Director advances violating section 185 in FY23/FY24 were repaid; FY26 ₹0.2945 cr was advanced and recovered during the year, so zero closing balance does not mean no related transaction. FY26 related enterprise purchases ₹8.8993 cr, related trade payables ₹1.6234 cr and loans ₹1.6814 cr are economically material. Director remuneration ₹2.1281 cr plus relative salary ₹0.2760 cr equals ₹2.4041 cr, 27.87% of restated PAT; director remuneration declined from ₹2.6921 cr in each previous year. The board’s arm’s-length assertion and 1 April 2025 Riansh noncompete/Annu exclusive arrangements are positive counterevidence, not independent market-price verification. Delivery record: motor relocation in September 2024 and FY26 production ramp occurred; 19 August 2026 construction start occurred; 16 October update still reports three operating units; Unit IV commissioning and award conversion remain future tests. No firm dated orderbook amount was retrieved, and no made-up missed deadline is recorded. These facts support GOV 4/EXEC 6 rather than fraud or an indiscriminate governance override.

sections.text:
Use the embedded six-year table with FY21–22 original and FY23–26 restated labels; do not stitch unreconciled older cash balances into a clean restated series. Adjustments include director-owned vehicles/loans, gratuity/leave accruals, MSME interest, subsidies and taxes. Recurring operating EBIT excludes other income: FY24 ₹3.7773 cr, FY25 ₹7.1253 cr, FY26 ₹12.3731 cr.

Three-year CFO ₹8.0902 cr versus PAT ₹15.8351 cr is 51.09%; deducting financing-classified interest yields 33.18%. FCF after cash capex is−₹12.9188 cr. Average receivable days 34.04→49.73→59.64 and material-cost cycle 36.89→60.50→75.18 show cash intensification. Closing FY26 AR ₹19.4333 cr has ₹0.4663 cr over 6 months including ₹0.0391 cr disputed over 3 years; most balances are recent, not proven bad debts.

Bank returns differ from books: FY24 Q4 stock+₹4.932 cr; FY25 Q4 stock+₹1.472 cr and debtors−₹3.6497 cr; FY26 Q2 debtors+₹1.6539 cr. Management cites unfinished entries and reconciliations. Importantly FY26 Q4 stock difference narrows to ₹0.0199 cr/0.1264%, while debtor difference−₹0.2518 cr remains. The FY26 CARO calls the stock difference immaterial.

FY25 audit-trail feature was not enabled throughout the year; completeness could not be concluded. FY26 main opinion and separate IFC are unmodified/adequate, yet Rule 11 text lacks an explicit audit-trail statement and contains an ambiguous reference to an EOM paragraph not visible in the main opinion. Absence of wording proves neither cure nor recurrence. G2 Hold is therefore about unresolved controls, not an allegation of fraud. FY26 CARO reports no default; small disputed tax items about ₹0.0732 cr are not a survival thesis.

Debt adjusted for uncleared CC cheques is ₹21.7669 cr; cheques reportedly cleared later. Tax asset ₹0.3788 cr, gratuity asset ₹0.0377 cr, subsidy receivable ₹1.1962 cr and restricted deposit ₹0.0314 cr are not freely spendable cash. Operating rental cost stays in margins with no double-counted AS19 lease liability.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the secondary ₹118.70 close, actual 12536218 shares imply ₹148.8049 cr equity value. FY26 restated earnings on the enlarged share count give EPS ₹6.8816/P/E 17.25×; original PAT gives 18.15×. Neither old weighted EPS ₹9.80 nor the prospectus comparison’s internally inconsistent own-company EPS ₹5.72/P/E 9.59 is used as current valuation. A historical March-debt EV/operating EBITDA diagnostic is 11.44×, not current EV because IPO cash and debt uses intervened.

The model separates actual May placement ₹3.3619 cr and IPO gross ₹32.3962 cr, estimated fees ₹3.2396 cr, earmarked capex ₹19.56 cr and debt repayment ₹4.7888 cr. remaining project spend, maintenance, growth capex, working capital, tax and interest are deducted once. total prepaids ₹0.6955 cr are not identified IPO expenses; fees are conservatively fully deducted, with a separately labeled maximum reimbursement sensitivity. capital creditors are unknown, tested at ₹2 cr; ₹0.0495 cr disclosed capital commitment sits within capex envelope. No optional warrants, acquisition, NCI or separate operational-land value is fabricated. Existing ₹14.4 cr CC is rolled in assumptions, not newly approved borrowing.

The consistent analyst reserve is max(₹1 cr,1% revenue run rate), applied from 31 March; opening actual cash fails it. This is a prudential continuity target, not proof of a historic default. Each interval checks cash before equity receipts, not just after; signed deficits remain. Actual post-listing cash/use-of-proceeds and availability remain unverified, so every ordinary and non-rescue conditional IRR/hurdle entry is null.

Fully separate rescue scenarios inject cash before needed, at 65% reference price with 5% fees, integer ceil shares and explicit dilution; pre-entry injections are historical counterfactuals, not actual capital events. Base rescue mechanical IRR 13.62%, bear−14.76% and bull 27.08% are not ordinary returns.

DCF uses 14/16/18% WACC,3/4/5% terminal growth,18% terminal ROIC and g/ROIC reinvestment, plus reserve growth; terminal cash retains required operations reserve. Discount exponents are actual days×5/1826, consistent with five-year terminal. FY32 stub uses 203/366 days; no post-terminal rescue can cure a prior gap.

Reverse expectations scans 0–60% constant growth for funded 12/15/18% crossings and reports none because the opening reserve fails. Two-way growth/multiple and cash/capex/customer stresses are fully embedded. Algebraic equity/DCF values are not investable targets, and no ordinary buy range is supplied.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is not simply that an SME multiple falls. One dominant customer can cut platform orders or shift sourcing while inventory, custom tools and fixed labor remain. Lower utilization compresses operating margin, collections slow, and a partly built plant still needs money. A linked stress reduces first-year revenue 30% (about 39% of the largest customer’s demand at unchanged others), starts EBIT margin 4%, raises core WC to sales 35%, overruns project 25% and exits at 6×EBIT. Algebraic terminal equity is ₹19.43/share before financing, not a recovery floor; separate rescue costs ₹2.7129 cr gross in the model and does not prove financing can be raised. Supplier/RPT support, CC renewal, capex deferral and inventory recovery could mitigate losses, but none is assumed to be an enforceable backstop. Operational property is already needed for enterprise earnings and is not added again as liquidation value. Thesis-break variables are dominant-customer volume/collections, inability to reconcile lender returns, or escalating committed spend without unrestricted funds. No actual default, lender fraud finding or proven inventory overstatement is asserted. Adverse recapitalization and market illiquidity can permanently impair a minority holder even if manufacturing survives.

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Feasibility
sections.text: A 5× share price gain over five years requires 37.97% CAGR; 10× requires 58.49%, before any dilution or taxes. At a 15× terminal P/E and no additional shares, a 5×₹118.70 price implies EPS ₹39.57 and PAT ₹49.60 cr; 10× implies EPS ₹79.13/PAT ₹99.20 cr. At a 10% net margin these require roughly ₹496/992 cr revenue, about 5.3×/10.6×FY26 sales. These are scale tests, not forecasts; sustained reinvestment, cash collection and customer diversification would also be necessary. Current near-full lines, ₹22.35 cr remaining project spend, 77.18% customer concentration and persistent poor cash conversion do not independently support that outcome. Larger peers demonstrate that automotive component scale is possible, not that LAPL will capture it. No 5×/10× designation is awarded, and using high multiple expansion or ignored rescue dilution would make the arithmetic less credible.

sections.text:
1. First published post-IPO balance and use-of-proceeds: reconcile ₹29.1566 cr net issue, ₹19.56 cr capex earmark, ₹4.7888 cr repayment and unpaid fees/capital creditors; do not infer unrestricted cash from gross issue.

2. Bank return reconciliation: close historical ₹4.932 cr stock / ₹3.6497 cr debtor differences and demonstrate current quarter agreement; preserve FY26 improvement.

3. Audit trail: obtain an explicit current-year edit log/test result and clarify FY26 Rule 11/EOM reference; silence is not resolution.

4. Collections: average AR days baseline 59.64; warn above 75 or aged >6 month amount doubling from ₹0.4663 cr.

5. Cash conversion: rolling three-year CFO/PAT baseline 51.09%, aim≥80% without temporary unpaid-supplier releases; watch after interest 33.18% separately.

6. Concentration: largest customer 77.18%, flag lost platform or share>80%; seek actual awards rather than vendor codes.

7. Capacity: motor 90.70%, lighting 91.25%, mirror 61.78%; track production, yields and rejection cost, not unweighted average alone.

8. Unit IV: FY27/FY28 IPO deployment ₹9.78 cr each, actual total cost/commissioning/qualification; flag>25% overrun or missing incremental cash return.

9. Governance: compounding order, director advances/RPT pricing and compensation trend; a clean filing is not retroactive proof.

10. Tradability: official sessions, lot 1200, current restrictions, no-print classification and spread before any implementation. These are research triggers, not automatic trade instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification is Hold — unresolved. Business Quality 5.3 and Growth Quality 5.0 are historical diagnostic assessments, not an eligible rank or compounder label. GOV 4,MOAT 5,DUR 6,CASH 3/BAL 5 fail the stronger compounder thresholds independently of IAS. IAS remains NS because R/P/L are unscored and G2/G3/G4 are unresolved. The appropriate action category is evidence-dependent watchlist, not buy/sell/short or a personalized allocation. A credible funding bridge and control closure could allow rerunning ordinary valuation with actual post-IPO shares/cash/debt; current price alone cannot do so. A downsidecase supported by audited current cash and confirmed bank drawing power would matter more than an optimistic announcement. Conversely an adverse auditor/lender finding, platform loss or severe execution miss would require reclassification. Historical operating strengths remain acknowledged and are not converted into an unsupported fraud verdict.

evidence.interpretation: Scored three-year normalized-period growth, not projected growth.

evidence.claim: Motor and lighting FY26 production 136058 and 205322 units/month; utilization 90.70% and 91.25%.
evidence.locator: Business capacity/production table; product revenue table
evidence.interpretation: Real volume scaling and near-capacity categories; new plant demand not assured.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Company 81.24% aggregate is an unweighted average of motor/lighting/mirror percentages, not a physical-unit-weighted utilization.

evidence.claim: Largest customer 77.18%; top 1095.49% of FY26 sales excluding other operating revenue.
evidence.locator: Risk factors/customer table
evidence.interpretation: Qualification relationships coexist with severe buyer concentration.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: No material customer default shown; top 10 share eased from 96.93% in FY24. Largest customer identity withheld, not inferred.

evidence.claim: FY24–26 cumulative CFO/PAT 51.09%; after financing interest 33.18%; cash capex FCF−₹12.9188 cr.
evidence.locator: F 6 cash flow; normalized definitions in model
evidence.interpretation: Persistent earnings-to-cash weakness, not capex deducted from CFO.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Most FY26 receivables under 6 months; expansion explains part, not three years of weak conversion.

evidence.claim: Average receivable days 34.04→49.73→59.64; material-basis cash-cycle proxy 36.89→60.50→75.18 days.
evidence.locator: F 4/F 5/F 6, material cost and inventories
evidence.interpretation: Cash intensity rises as volumes expand; closing AR days 76.07.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Proxy uses material cost, not fully allocated production cost; no precise SKU/customer cash cycle disclosed.

evidence.claim: FY26 adjusted debt ₹21.7669 cr includes ₹0.7775 cr uncleared CC cheques; cash ₹0.1927 cr; EBIT/interest 7.04×.
evidence.locator: F 4, borrowings/current liability note; CARO default clause
evidence.interpretation: Historical leverage manageable on EBIT, but drawn CC and thin cash constrain flexibility.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Auditor no-default finding and subsequent cheque clearance are preserved; no actual insolvency asserted.

evidence.claim: FY26 restated PAT ₹8.6269 cr versus original ₹8.1993 cr; net increase ₹0.4276 cr.
evidence.locator: F 11–14 restatement bridges
evidence.interpretation: Prior-period reallocation and small tax net adjustment explain arithmetic, but controls require separate review.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: A disclosed restatement is not itself fraud; recurring FY26 operating EBIT ₹12.3731 cr excludes other income.

evidence.claim: Quarterly stock / book-debt bank returns differ from books; FY24 Q4 stock+₹4.9320 cr; FY25 Q4 debtors−₹3.6497 cr; FY26 Q2 debtors+₹1.6539 cr.
evidence.locator: F 46–47; FY26 CARO p 39; FY25 CARO
evidence.interpretation: Reconciliation/control issue is material across periods.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Issuer explains incomplete entries/reconciliation in process. FY26 Q4 stock difference narrowed to ₹0.0199 cr (0.1264%); debtor difference−₹0.2518 cr remains. No lender loss established.

evidence.claim: FY25 audit-trail software/feature not enabled throughout year; auditor unable to conclude completeness; separate IFC adequate/effective.
evidence.locator: FY25 main audit p 5 and IFC p 14; FY26 pp 33–46
evidence.interpretation: Unmodified opinion and clean IFC do not erase specific audit-trail exception.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: FY26 Rule 11 pages do not state an explicit audit-trail conclusion; silence is neither proof of cure nor proof of repeated failure. FY26 main/IFC remain unmodified.

evidence.claim: Historic allotment/rights compliance lapses disclosed; compounding application 16 May 2026 pending at prospectus; director advances repaid.
evidence.locator: Risk factors/capital history; DRHP examiner F 2; related-party notes
evidence.interpretation: Repeated compliance failures justify GOV 4, not an unsupported severe-diversion finding.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Management describes inadvertent oversight and corrective filings. No completed compounding order found; FY26 ₹0.2945 cr director advances issued/repaid, zero year-end is not zero activity.

evidence.claim: FY26 related purchases ₹8.8993 cr; director pay ₹2.1281 cr; relative salary ₹0.2760 cr; related loans ₹1.6814 cr.
evidence.locator: F 36–38 related-party transactions
evidence.interpretation: Commercial related parties and family compensation merit arm’s-length scrutiny.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Remuneration fell from ₹2.6921 cr in FY24/25; company asserts arm’s-length dealing and signed noncompete/exclusive agreements 1 April 2025. Neither assertion proves abusive conduct.

evidence.claim: Three-year ΔNOPAT ₹8.114175 cr/Δcore operating IC ₹33.063 cr=24.54%; two-year 27.74%.
evidence.locator: Derived restated financial bridge, model incremental_return_bridges
evidence.interpretation: Stable organic perimeter supports CAP 7 as an accounting-based substitute for unavailable project cohorts.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Alternative funded-capital returns 25.34%/26.49%; cash-capex bridge residual−₹0.1725 cr remains. Not a Unit IV IRR or through-cycle guarantee.

evidence.claim: May placement ₹3.3618888 cr; IPO gross ₹32.39616 cr; net ₹29.15656 cr after estimated fees.
evidence.locator: Capital history/objects/allotment; current issued capital
evidence.interpretation: Real capital raising improves resources; post-issue available balances still unverified.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: ₹19.56 cr is earmarked capex, ₹4.7888 cr debt repayment; not all net proceeds are free cash. Fees rounded; IPO dates do not prove cash unspent.

evidence.claim: Unit IV remaining project spend ₹22.3549 cr, plus ₹3.5932 cr already-paid land; IPO capex deployment FY27/28₹9.78 cr each.
evidence.locator: Objects and 19 August construction release
evidence.interpretation: Expansion addresses capacity tightness; internal/debt contribution ₹2.7949 cr plus tax/extras needs funding.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Vendor quotes are not binding orders; construction start is not commissioning; 16 October still describes three operating units.

evidence.claim: Three new vendor codes and new EV/lighting products are disclosed, without firm minimum-order value.
evidence.locator: Business announcements
evidence.interpretation: RFQ eligibility and product capability can diversify but cannot be booked as guaranteed growth.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Existing operating volume growth provides concrete execution evidence; future awards remain uncertain.
